nh_gem_hunter.blurb: Gem Hunter is a small cliff perched high on the eastern side of Rattlesnake Mountain at Rumney, and you can spot it from Stinson Lake Road. It holds a dozen routes, almost all of them bolted sport lines plus a single trad line, on schist. Expect mostly 5.7 to 5.10 climbing with a couple of 5.11s, so it suits moderate climbers more than hard-core projectors. The wall faces east and catches the sun and sees far fewer people than the big Rumney crags, though the steep, flagged walk up is a workout and the routes can be webbed with spiders.

nh_1_the_motherlode.blurb: The Motherlode is the southernmost wall at North Bald Cap, an ice and mixed crag in the far north of New Hampshire, found past the big slabs on the left. It is a long, steep face hung with free-standing icicles, some touching the ground, and it offers short, steep single-pitch lines. Of the dozen climbs, most are ice in the WI4 to WI5 range, with a few harder pitches reaching WI6, and one mixed route. Reaching the cliff is a backcountry trip, and deep snow may call for snowshoes or skis, so plan it as a committed winter day rather than a quick roadside lap.

nh_lakeside_crag.blurb: Lakeside Crag is a small cliff in Pawtuckaway State Park looking out over Round Pond. It is mostly a crack-climbing venue, with eight trad lines and four top-rope problems running from an easy scramble up to a thin 5.12 crack, so beginners and leaders alike can find something. Most of the grades cluster in the 5.7 to 5.10 range. Anchors for top-roping are simple to build from the pines on the rim. It draws fewer people than the main Pawtuckaway cliffs, and unlike most of the surrounding shaded rock it gets enough sun to be climbable in the middle of winter.

nh_45_to_life_area.blurb: The 45 To Life Area is a cluster of boulders in the Hillside section of Pawtuckaway State Park, near the point where the trail heads off toward the Lower Slabs. The terrain is steep, with overhanging walls and some highball problems. Twelve problems are logged here, and most are easy to moderate, between V0 and V3. A handful of much harder lines climb up to V9 for strong boulderers, which makes it a fair stop for a mixed group. Fido at V5 and Mantlepiece at V1 are among the most popular, and Hillside as a whole is rarely crowded.

nh_safe_space.blurb: Safe Space is a small zone of crags in Merriam Woods, the Russell Crags area near Woodstock, built around a cracked buttress at the top of the right-hand gully. Unusually for Russell, it blends six sport routes with six trad lines. The taller central section runs about 70 to 80 feet and is mostly 5.10 and 5.11, while the ends hold shorter lines, including a 5.7 on the right. The central rock is described as fragile and a bit vegetated in places, and the bolted lines were placed with stick clips in mind, so bring one. It feels relaxed and out of the way.

nh_downing_mountain_eagle_cliff.blurb: Downing Mountain, also called Eagle Cliff, is a winter ice and mixed venue near Rumney, where a band of small crags runs along the southern flank above Stinson Lake. The twelve climbs are short: easy and moderate ice from about WI2 to WI4, plus mixed lines in the M3 to M6 range. Some of the ice stands 20 feet or more, but so far it has only been climbed without a rope, so climbers should place tools carefully and carry a short rope. It is a modest, low-key spot for quick laps or learning to swing tools rather than a full day of long pitches.

nh_4_mt_webster_winter_ice_mixed.blurb: Mt. Webster in winter offers long, moderate gullies on the mountain's west slope, facing Mt. Willey across Crawford Notch. About a dozen routes are listed, mostly ice from WI2 to WI4, with a couple of mixed gully lines that finish on rock, such as Shoestring Gully and Green Chasm. The climbing is alpine in feel, with snow and ice combined and views down the notch, so it suits parties comfortable with route-finding and avalanche assessment. Beginners can find low-angle WI2 gullies here, while Heart Palace gives a steeper challenge. Reaching the climbs involves crossing the Saco River.

nh_numb_thumb_area.blurb: The Numb Thumb Area is part of the Devil's Den boulders in Pawtuckaway State Park. The focus is one huge block on an earthen base on the slope right of the Ashes to Ashes boulders, ringed by smaller rocks. There are twelve problems, mostly V1 to V5, which makes it friendly to climbers of moderate strength, while the namesake line, Numb Thumb, is a three-star V7. Two of the easier problems carry a PG13 warning. Devil's Den as a whole sees little traffic, so expect moss and lichen on some of the easier lines.
